messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: High error/queue growth for dedicated pool 'eu-dedicated-1' affecting reserved enterprise tenants. Severity: P1. Paging oncall (Sam).

Sam (oncall): I'm on it. seeing alerts for queue length and Throttles spike. Checking pool dashboard now.

Priya (sre): I can help with scaling checks. Any autoscaler errors?

Sam (oncall): Autoscaler logs show failures trying to add nodes. suspect quota / scale limit. Pulling logs.

Miguel (ml-runtime): Customer reports timeouts for heavy-inference tenants. Which tenants are reserved on this pool?

Dotan (runtime): Reserved tenants: tenant-acme, tenant-velox, tenant-42 (internal test). Reserved GPUs appear fully allocated. Noisy metrics show tenant-42 spiking usage.

Sam (oncall): Confirmed. queue_length ~ 280 and growing; reserved_gpu_utilization 100%. Throttle rate increasing, many requests hitting 429.

Priya (sre): Pasting recent autoscaler error block:
```
ERROR autoscaler.controller: failed to scale up: quota_exceeded: cannot provision additional GPU nodes in eu-west-1
pool_id=eu-dedicated-1 desired_nodes=18 current_nodes=16 max_nodes=16
queue_length=280 reserved_gpu_usage=100% noisy_tenant=tenant-42
```

Alex (infra): Cloud provider shows quota cap on vGPUs for that region for our subscription. We hit the hard limit. We can request quota increase but that's not instant.

Miguel (ml-runtime): So autoscaler is blocked by cloud quota. Meanwhile noisy tenant-42 is consuming reserved GPUs meant for tenant-acme and tenant-velox?

Dotan (runtime): tenant-42 is on a reserved slot (shared dev reservation) but ramped to heavy batch jobs unexpectedly. Looks like a runaway batch job.

Sam (oncall): Immediate mitigations proposals: 1) Throttle tenant-42 down to cap. 2) Apply temporary per-reservation rate limits for enterprise tenants to relieve queue. 3) Failover heavy requests to smaller model variants (fp16->int8) if acceptable. 4) Contact account-eng / CS to notify impacted customers. Opinions?

Priya (sre): +1 to throttling noisy tenant and per-reservation limits. I'll prepare a controlled throttling policy.

Alex (infra): I can open an emergency quota increase request but won't be approved in <1h. We should assume quota won't arrive fast enough.

Jess (customer-success): I'll draft a short customer note for tenant-acme and tenant-velox explaining we're applying temporary rate limits and fallbacks; no data was lost. Need exact ETA and what we throttle.

account-eng: Hold off external comms until we know impact window; we should be clear about degraded throughput not data loss.

Sam (oncall): Executing throttling for tenant-42 now. Command:
```
# limit tenant-42 to 10tps on eu-dedicated-1
rictl reservation update --tenant tenant-42 --pool eu-dedicated-1 --rps 10
```

Sam (oncall): Throttle applied. Monitoring queue.

Priya (sre): Applying soft per-reservation limit for enterprise reservations: 50rps per reservation while we stabilize.

Dotan (runtime): Pushing a lightweight fallback policy to route requests that exceed latency SLO to int8 model variant for tenant-acme. This will reduce GPU memory and throughput pressure.

Miguel (ml-runtime): How many requests can we shed by model downgrade? Rough estimate: 30-40% token throughput reduction.

Sam (oncall): Queue dropped from 280 -> 120 in ~6 minutes after throttle + fallback. Throttles still present but trending down.

Priya (sre): We're observing some degraded tail latency for long-context calls. We should keep throttles until queue stays <50 for 10m.

Jess (customer-success): Drafted message to customers: "We're experiencing degraded performance on your dedicated pool due to capacity exhaustion. We've applied temporary rate limits and fallbacks; no data was lost. We'll update in 30 minutes." Want to add anything?

account-eng: Add that we're prioritizing committed reserved capacity first, and that we're opening an internal ticket for quota increase and noisy-tenant root cause.

Alex (infra): I've raised the emergency quota request with cloud and referenced ticket #CLOUD-47291. No guarantee on timing.

Dotan (runtime): Root cause tracing: tenant-42 batch job didn't set concurrency cap, spawned many concurrent long-context requests. We have an eval rule that should have caught this; seems it was bypassed in their dev reservation.

Miguel (ml-runtime): We'll add an automatic circuit to detect sudden sustained reservation usage >80% and auto-apply short-term caps next deploy. Postmortem action.

Sam (oncall): Current status: queue=42 reserved_gpu_util=92% throttles active for tenant-42 and soft caps in place for enterprise reservations. Autoscaler still blocked by cloud quota.

Priya (sre): Next steps for oncall: 1) Keep throttles until stable <50 for 10m. 2) Coordinate with infra for quota and possible manual migration of some non-reserved workloads to burst pool. 3) Capture logs for postmortem.

Jess (customer-success): Sent customer note to tenant-acme and tenant-velox. Waiting on replies.

account-eng: I'll coordinate account outreach if customers escalate.

Sam (oncall): Handoff to Priya for next 2h watch. I'm logging incident start and will draft incident timeline.

Priya (sre): Acknowledged. I'll monitor and update every 15m. If queue rises >120 again, escalate to SRE lead for potential broader mitigations.

incident-bot: Incident auto-update: status=investigating; severity=P1; owners=[Priya (sre)]; lead=Sam (oncall).

Sam (oncall): Adding quick logs dump for postmortem capture:
```
metrics snapshot: {
  "pool": "eu-dedicated-1",
  "timestamp": "1799991111",
  "desired_nodes": 18,
  "current_nodes": 16,
  "max_nodes": 16,
  "queue_length": 312,
  "reserved_usage_pct": 100,
  "noisy_tenant": "tenant-42"
}
```

Priya (sre): Closing note: stabilization looks good. Will keep incident channel open for 2h watch and then milestone to postmortem.

Miguel (ml-runtime): Filing follow-up: add automatic reservation caps, improve dev-reservation guardrails, telemetry alert for rapid reservation ramp.

Jess (customer-success): Customers acknowledged; one asked for a post-incident summary. Will coordinate with account-eng and Sam.

Sam (oncall): End of immediate mitigation. Handing incident to Priya for monitoring and postmortem ownership.

Priya (sre): Taking ownership. Marking last_message_ts and will update postmortem once incident timeline is compiled."
